story.title: FBI Executes Search Warrant at Eric Swalwell's Home in Misconduct Investigation
story.summary: Federal agents executed search warrants at the home of former Representative Eric Swalwell, seizing electronic devices as part of an investigation into allegations of sexual misconduct. The search took place on a Sunday morning, according to sources familiar with the matter.

explore_lenses.label: What does the FBI search establish—and not establish?
explore_lenses.title: A warrant signals an active probe, not a charge
explore_lenses.summary: The searches show that a criminal investigation has progressed to court-authorized evidence collection. They do not by themselves establish that Swalwell committed a crime or that prosecutors will bring charges.

claims.text: CBS News reported that agents executed warrants at San Francisco International Airport and Swalwell's Washington, D.C., residence, and that a court filing listed an iPhone and MacBook Pro among the property seized.

Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 41 requires officers executing a property-search warrant to prepare an inventory, provide or leave a warrant copy and receipt, and promptly return the warrant and inventory to the designated magistrate judge.
No criminal charge against Swalwell was reported in the supplied CBS or ABC accounts as of August 21, 2026.

explore_lenses.label: How did the investigation reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: It follows allegations, local inquiry, and resignation
explore_lenses.summary: The federal searches come after public allegations from several women, a local sheriff's investigation into one allegation, and Swalwell's April resignation from Congress. Those earlier developments involved separate political, ethics, and law-enforcement tracks.

claims.text: ABC News reported that Lonna Drewes publicly alleged in April that Swalwell raped her in 2018, and that the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said it was opening an investigation into her allegation; ABC said it had not independently verified the accusation.
Swalwell's lawyer, Sara Azari, said he categorically denied all sexual-misconduct and assault allegations and characterized them as a political campaign against him.

Swalwell resigned from Congress on April 14 after the House Ethics Committee announced an investigation; his resignation letter acknowledged unspecified mistakes in judgment while calling the serious allegation false.

The House Ethics Committee says its investigative jurisdiction covers House Members, officers, and employees, which helps explain why the congressional ethics process no longer provides an ongoing forum once a member leaves office.

explore_lenses.label: What are the key next legal steps?
explore_lenses.title: Investigators will review devices; charging remains unresolved
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate next stage is likely forensic review and analysis of the seized devices under the warrant's terms. Prosecutors would then have to decide whether the evidence supports charges, while Swalwell can challenge an unlawful seizure through court procedures.

claims.text: CBS News reported, based on sources familiar with the inquiry, that investigators were examining a possible federal civil-rights theory under 18 U.S.C. § 242; that report did not say Swalwell had been charged under the statute.

The Justice Department describes 18 U.S.C. § 242 as prohibiting a person acting under color of law from willfully depriving someone of a constitutional or legal right; whether that provision applies to these facts has not been publicly established.
Rule 41 permits a person claiming an unlawful search or deprivation of property to seek its return, and permits a defendant to seek suppression of evidence in the trial court.

story_report.summary: FBI agents executed search warrants connected to former Rep. Eric Swalwell, seizing electronic devices in a federal investigation involving allegations of sexual misconduct. CBS News reported that agents searched Swalwell at San Francisco International Airport and his Washington, D.C., residence; a court filing listed an iPhone and MacBook Pro among the seized property. No criminal charge against Swalwell was reported in the supplied CBS or ABC accounts as of Aug. 21, 2026.

sections.heading: Swalwell Allegations and Congressional Resignation
sections.body: ABC News reported that Lonna Drewes publicly alleged in April that Swalwell raped her in 2018, an accusation ABC said it had not independently verified. The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said it was opening an investigation into her allegation. Swalwell resigned from Congress on April 14 after the House Ethics Committee announced an investigation, acknowledging unspecified mistakes in judgment while calling the serious allegation false.

sections.heading: Swalwell Denies Sexual-Misconduct Allegations
sections.body: Swalwell’s lawyer, Sara Azari, said he categorically denied all allegations of sexual misconduct and assault, characterizing them as part of a political campaign against him. The reporting reviewed does not establish whether the FBI inquiry stems from Drewes’ allegation, another allegation, or evidence from a separate investigative referral.

sections.heading: Federal Inquiry Has No Public Timeline
sections.body: CBS News, citing sources familiar with the inquiry, reported that investigators were examining a possible federal civil-rights theory under 18 U.S.C. § 242. The Justice Department describes that statute as barring willful deprivation of rights by someone acting under color of law, but its applicability to these facts has not been publicly established. Rule 41 also provides procedures for warrant inventories and potential challenges seeking return or suppression of seized evidence.

unresolved.text: The warrants, supporting affidavits and precise evidentiary basis for the federal investigation have not been publicly detailed in the reporting reviewed.

related_stories.title: New York Woman Charged with Terrorism for Alleged Capitol Bomb Plot
related_stories.summary: A 35-year-old woman has been charged with a terrorism offense for allegedly plotting to bomb the New York State Capitol. Jessica Bowie reportedly expressed a desire to destroy the Capitol buildings to an FBI informant, leading to her arrest in a sting operation. The charges are linked to her alleged support for the Islamic State (ISIS) group.

related_stories.summary: The Central African Republic has shut down the Zamboye artisanal gold mine following a landslide that resulted in at least 49 confirmed deaths. Local sources suggest the death toll may be as high as 100, with many miners still unaccounted for.

related_stories.title: Eight Killed in Charter Plane Crash at Military Radar Site in Alaska
related_stories.summary: A charter plane carrying eight people crashed near a U.S. military-managed radar site in western Alaska, resulting in the deaths of all on board. The plane, a Cessna 441, reportedly went down on approach to Cape Newenham. An investigation into the incident is currently underway.

related_stories.title: Personalized mRNA Cancer Treatment Shows Promise Against Melanoma in Trial
related_stories.summary: Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer treatment has successfully reduced melanoma tumor recurrence in a late-stage clinical trial. This marks a significant milestone in cancer treatment, as it is the first time an mRNA-based drug has shown positive results in such a large trial. Researchers are optimistic about the potential for this approach to be applied to other types of cancer in the future.
